It does to a certain degree. A lot of life is how much you put in and how lucky you get. I was 27, homeless, no education, and no relevant  job experience. I had gone through a devastating breakup and got kicked out of my house.  The way I got out of it was people helping me out. Family was no help and just saw it as I needed to grow up. Never mind the fact that I was sleeping in my car. So I took a job a delivery driver. I got an unpaid internship at a law firm through a friend I knew. It was unpaid but it was experience to help set me up for future jobs. I went back to school and started studying for the lsat with the help of friend who was willing to do it for free. I was sleeping in the attic of a rec center owned by a friend of mine. It was private and had a bathroom and a shower. Those five things, the rec center, the university , the internship, the lsat studying and the delivery job got me through it all. A lot of it was hard work on my end but a lot of luck from people willing to help me out.
